name: Isles of Scilly

council.name: Council of the Isles of Scilly

licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme: national mandatory licensing applies, for homes let to five or more people from two or more households sharing facilities, which on Scilly often includes staff accommodation. The council keeps a public register of licensed HMOs.

privateRentedShare.text: 36.6% of households rent privately (Census 2021), up from 29.7% in 2011; the ONS advises care with comparisons because the population is small

councilTax.text: £2,047.96 Band D (2026/27), including the police precept; the council's own share is £1,744.76

housing: The Isles of Scilly have the highest share of private renting outside London, at more than a third of households in 2021, much of it let by the Duchy of Cornwall, which owns most of the land. Homes are mostly granite cottages, terraces and farmhouses, and a large part of the housing is used for holiday lets or staff accommodation for the tourism season, which makes year-round homes scarce. Shared staff housing often needs an HMO licence.
checkinTips: Granite cottages exposed to Atlantic weather: look for damp on thick walls, salt corrosion on window frames and door furniture, and storm damage to roofs.
Shared staff accommodation: photograph each room's lock and furniture, fire doors, alarms and the kitchen, and note the HMO licence if there is one.
Homes off the mains gas network: photograph the heating system, oil or LPG tank and gauge, and any private water supply or septic tank.
Furnished seasonal lets: list and photograph every item of furniture and kitchen equipment, as replacements are hard to get on the islands.
Low-lying homes in Hugh Town: look for signs of past flooding from storm surges in ground-floor rooms.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact the Council of the Isles of Scilly's environmental health team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
